overall_summary: Analysis of recent performance indicates that space and astronomy topics utilizing high-stakes 'What If' scenarios and extreme planetary descriptions (e.g., diamond planets, extreme darkness, unusual orbits) drive significantly higher views and engagement ratios compared to psychological or general biological facts. Videos published within the last 30 days show clear breakout performance when framing bizarre cosmic realities around immersive hypothetical questions.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views) demonstrate superior engagement velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form content focusing on hypothetical survival or interaction with extreme astronomical anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal phenomena such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views) capture strong initial curiosity and watch time.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight counter-intuitive physical properties of celestial bodies using bold numeric or comparative hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics centered around internal cognitive tricks like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' underperformed severely (ranging from 5 to 53 views across multiple iterations).
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological facts and personal cognitive hacks in favor of external, visually arresting science and space concepts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Directly repeating similar facts without a fresh narrative angle (e.g., multiple octopus heart shorts with diminishing returns) leads to stagnant view counts.
weak_patterns.action: Ensure strict novelty checking before production; avoid re-covering biological trivia unless paired with a completely novel cinematic presentation.
